name: Vijay Darda
current_role: Chairman, Lokmat Media Group (Lokmat newspapers, Nagpur/Mumbai); former Rajya Sabha MP (1998-2016)
profile: Vijay Jawaharlal Darda (b. 1950, Yavatmal) is the elder son of freedom fighter Jawaharlal Darda, who launched the Marathi daily Lokmat in 1971. He built Lokmat into a multi-language media group and served three Rajya Sabha terms for Maharashtra. He remains group chairman, writes columns and has published books such as 'Ringside' (2023) and 'The Churn' (2025).
interesting_fact: He won his first Rajya Sabha seat in 1998 as an independent, defeating the official Congress candidate, before Congress nominated him for the 2004 and 2010 terms.
deep_cut_fact: His long-running 'dream project' is the 284 km Wardha-Yavatmal-Nanded railway line serving his home district; by 2021 he said he had pursued it for 13 years and discussed it with eleven Railway Ministers.
notes: Active on social media and writes regularly, so reachable via his site/X. Be aware he and his son were defendants in a coal-block allocation case (2023 conviction reported, later acquittal reported by Lokmat Times); avoid the topic.

name: Wu Guicun
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2010) with an estimated US$150m, wealth attributed to Yinghua Pharmaceuticals (pharmaceutical wholesale). No English or accessible Chinese-language sources could be found confirming his current role or the company details.
notes: Very low public profile; web searches in English and Chinese (武贵存 英华医药) returned nothing verifiable. Would need Chinese business-registry research (e.g. National Enterprise Credit Information System) to locate the company.

name: Sheela Ashwin Chiniwalla
profile: Listed on the Hurun India Rich List (2018-2019) with about US$132m, wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) owned by the Chauhan family. Presumably a Chauhan family member/shareholder; no public profile found and she is not among the listed directors of Parle Products.
notes: Private family shareholder with no public footprint found. Parle Products current directors are Vijay, Ajay, Arup and Samar Chauhan; any approach would realistically go via the company (parleproducts.com).

name: Liang Peitang
current_role: Listed as contact/principal of Guangdong Dadi Communications Chain Service Co., Ltd. (per D&B directory)
profile: Founder/owner associated with Dadi Communications (大地通讯), a Guangdong mobile-phone retail chain; listed on the Hurun China Rich List in 2007-2008 with about US$130m. Little else is published about him in accessible sources.
notes: A D&B business directory lists "Peitang Liang" as contact for Guangdong Dadi Communications Chain Service Co Ltd (https://www.dnb.com/business-directory/company-profiles.guangdong_dadi_communications_chain_service_co_ltd.3d257bfe9b5b5d5d431581732c31c00d.html). No press or personal channels found; very low profile.

name: Zhang Chunwang
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2005-2008) with about US$120m, wealth attributed to Xinwang Group (aluminium materials). No accessible English or Chinese sources could be found confirming his current role.
notes: No verifiable public footprint found (searches for 张春旺 新旺集团 returned nothing relevant). Do not confuse with Zhang Shiping/Zhang Bo (Weiqiao/Hongqiao) or China Zhongwang.

name: Ruan Xiwei
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2002-2006) with about US$100m, wealth attributed to Deya Group (investment, agriculture, real estate). No accessible sources found confirming current activities.
notes: No verifiable public footprint found in English or Chinese searches (阮希玮 德亚集团). Last appeared on a rich list in 2006.

name: Morgan Freeman
current_role: Actor, narrator and co-founder of Revelations Entertainment (production company, with Lori McCreary); currently stars in Paramount+'s 'Lioness'
profile: Oscar-winning American actor (b. 1937, Memphis; raised in Mississippi) known for 'The Shawshank Redemption', 'Million Dollar Baby' and as one of the most recognisable narrators in film and documentary ('March of the Penguins', 'Through the Wormhole'). His wealth comes from five decades of film work and Revelations Entertainment. Nearing 90, he says he has no plans to retire and released a blues album in August 2026.
interesting_fact: After high school he turned down a partial drama scholarship to Jackson State and enlisted in the US Air Force, serving as an automatic tracking radar repairman and rising to airman first class.
deep_cut_fact: He named his production company Revelations Entertainment because he wanted to 'reveal hidden truths' and improve African-American representation on screen; he started it with Lori McCreary, the producer of his directorial debut 'Bopha!' (1993), while filming 'Outbreak'.
notes: Not an entrepreneur in the usual sense; the business angle is Revelations Entertainment (co-run by Lori McCreary, who is active on X/Instagram and is likely the better first contact). Media requests normally go via his talent agency/publicist.

name: Ashok Sarin
current_role: Deceased (was Executive Chairman and founder of Anant Raj Ltd)
profile: Founder (1969) of the Delhi real-estate group Anant Raj Ltd; served as Executive Chairman until his death on 22 August 2021. The company is now led by the next generation (Aman Sarin, CEO) alongside Anil Sarin.
notes: Died 22 Aug 2021 per Anant Raj's stock-exchange intimation: https://bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/ac95e740-007e-4694-9b97-89aed63d7ce7.pdf . Wealth was shared with brother Anil Sarin; for Anant Raj (now pushing into data centres) approach Aman/Anil Sarin.

name: Philip R Gallagher
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Avnet Inc. (since Nov 2020); director, Dycom Industries
profile: Phil Gallagher is a Drexel graduate from South Jersey who joined Hamilton Avnet in 1982 and has spent almost his whole career at the Phoenix-based electronic components distributor, running Electronics Marketing Americas and Technology Solutions before a stint at TTI. He returned in 2017 to run Electronic Components and became CEO in 2020; his wealth is mainly Avnet equity.
interesting_fact: He joined Avnet in 1982 in a 100%-commission sales job with no electronics background after a lunch with an Avnet employee: 'I didn't know anything about electronics ... and I'm still learning after 40 years.'
deep_cut_fact: As a teen he pumped gas at a Hess station, and his first resume described the job as 'petroleum transferring agent'; he was also a college nose guard whom a coach once said was too small to make varsity.
notes: Press contact Liam Creighton is named in Avnet's 2026 press releases. Avnet is moving its HQ from Phoenix to Tempe in 2026. Relevant to the podcast via electronics/semiconductor supply chain for data centres.

name: Luther King Jr
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Luther King Capital Management (Fort Worth); independent director, TXO Partners L.P.
profile: J. Luther King Jr., CFA, born in Odessa, Texas, founded Fort Worth investment adviser Luther King Capital Management in 1979 (about $30.5bn AUM in late 2025). He is a director and roughly 8% unitholder of oil and gas producer TXO Partners, has served on five public boards (incl. Tyler Technologies) and chaired TCU's board of trustees.
interesting_fact: He started LKCM in 1979 after declining to relocate to New York when his employer, Lionel D. Edie & Company (where he ran the Dallas office), was sold. He was inducted into the Texas Business Hall of Fame in October 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1963 as a credit analyst at First National Bank of Fort Worth, and in 2002 established the LKCM Center for Financial Studies at TCU's Neeley School of Business, his alma mater (BSC and MBA).

public_contacts.value: https://www.lkcm.com/about/contact-lkcm/ (firm office contact page; Fort Worth office main line 817.332.3235)

notes: Not to be confused with Martin Luther King Jr. Energy angle: major TXO Partners (oil & gas) holder alongside his firm. Best route is via LKCM's Fort Worth office.

name: Giuseppina Albo
current_role: Group Chief Executive Officer, Hamilton Insurance Group, Ltd. (NYSE: HG, Bermuda) since January 2018
profile: Pina Albo is a Canadian-trained lawyer who spent about 25 years at Munich Re, rising from claims expert to its Board of Executive Management (P&C Europe and Latin America). She succeeded founder Brian Duperreault as CEO of Bermuda-based specialty insurer/reinsurer Hamilton in 2018 and took it public on the NYSE in 2023; her wealth is largely Hamilton equity.
interesting_fact: She began her career practising real estate, corporate finance and M&A law in Toronto before switching to insurance as a claims expert at Munich Re.
deep_cut_fact: Before law school at Osgoode Hall she earned a BA in Languages from the University of Winnipeg, and she also holds a Maitrise en Droit in international and European Community law from Universite d'Aix-Marseille III in Aix-en-Provence.
notes: Goes by 'Pina'. Media contact is Kelly Corday Ferris; IR is Darian Niforatos. Advocate for women in insurance (ambassador, Insurance Supper Club); NIC Canada keynote speaker.

name: Steven D Hovde
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Hovde Group (bank-focused investment bank); director and 10% owner, Coastal Financial Corp (CCB); chairman, Hovde Properties
profile: Steve Hovde co-founded Hovde Group in 1987, a boutique investment bank advising banks and thrifts on capital raising and M&A, and opened its Chicago office in 1988. He invests in banks alongside his brother Eric (controlling interest in Sunwest Bank; major holder of Seattle-area Coastal Financial, on whose board he has sat since 2011) and chairs Madison-based Hovde Properties.
interesting_fact: Before investment banking he was a CPA at Touche Ross in Chicago, then a real-estate lawyer at Rudnick & Wolfe (now DLA Piper), then regional general counsel of developer Vantage Companies.
deep_cut_fact: With his brother Eric he backs the Hovde Foundation, whose 'Hovde Homes' partner with children's homes in countries including Bolivia, Ghana, Malawi, Peru and Rwanda; it reports $19M+ granted to 170+ nonprofit partners.
notes: Law degree (cum laude) from Northwestern, BBA accounting from UW-Madison. Brother Eric Hovde is a political figure; keep outreach business-focused (bank M&A, fintech/BaaS via Coastal's CCBX).

name: Richard Barry
current_role: President & CEO, Cassava Sciences (SAVA); independent director, Sarepta Therapeutics (since 2015)
profile: Rick Barry is a former hedge-fund manager: a portfolio manager and managing director at Robertson Stephens Investment Management, then a founding managing general partner of Eastbourne Capital Management (1999-2010), a large equity fund with healthcare exposure. He has sat on Sarepta's board since 2015 and moved from Cassava's board (2021) to executive chairman and then CEO, now steering it towards TSC-related epilepsy.
interesting_fact: He was a partner and advisory board member of Major League Baseball's San Diego Padres from 2009 to 2021.
deep_cut_fact: A Penn State BA, he previously served on the advisory board of Penn State's Schreyer Honors College.
notes: Goes by 'Rick'. Best business route is via Cassava Sciences (Austin, TX) investor relations; no published personal channels found. Biotech investor, not energy.

name: Brandon Taylor Mintz
current_role: Founder and non-executive director (and adviser to the CEO), Bitcoin Depot Inc. (NASDAQ: BTM), Atlanta
profile: Brandon Mintz founded Atlanta-based Bitcoin Depot in 2016 after a first crypto venture, Cash To Crypto, started while he was at the University of Georgia. He built it into one of the largest bitcoin ATM networks in North America and took it public on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2023, serving as CEO and later executive chairman. In March 2026 he stepped back to a non-executive board seat as ex-MoneyGram chief Alex Holmes became chairman & CEO.
interesting_fact: He said he started Bitcoin Depot after personally finding it 'really difficult and cumbersome' to buy bitcoin online, and realising buying with cash was far simpler, which led to the cash-to-bitcoin kiosk model.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from UGA he wound down his first company, OTC crypto desk Cash To Crypto, and used his own savings to launch Bitcoin Depot in summer 2016; UGA's Terry College profiled the 2023 Nasdaq listing as 'a decade in the making'.

public_contacts.value: Gateway Group (Investors & Media for Bitcoin Depot): BTM@gateway-grp.com, 949-574-3860

notes: Young founder (UGA grad). Company under heavy state regulatory pressure on crypto ATMs in 2026; keep outreach on the founding story. Has written for Bitcoin Magazine and appeared on several podcasts, so likely receptive to interviews.

name: Jennifer Anne Garner
current_role: Actress; co-founder, director and spokesperson ('Farmer Jen'), Once Upon a Farm PBC (NYSE: OFRM)
profile: Jennifer Garner (b. 1972) is the American actress known for 'Alias' and '13 Going on 30'. In 2017 she joined founder Cassandra Curtis and ex-Annie's CEO John Foraker as co-founder of organic kids' food brand Once Upon a Farm, which listed on the NYSE in February 2026, raising about $198m at a ~$724m valuation. She sits on its board and remains its public face.
interesting_fact: She ties Once Upon a Farm's mission to her long-running work as a Save the Children ambassador; before the February 2026 NYSE listing she told Fortune the team 'probably slept an hour each'.
deep_cut_fact: She bought her mother's family farm near Locust Grove, Oklahoma, which her grandparents purchased in 1936 with her grandfather's WWI veteran's bonus, and is converting it to a working organic farm that feeds into Once Upon a Farm's supply chain.

public_contacts.value: OFARMPR@icrinc.com (ICR, media contacts Jessica Liddell / Kate Schneiderman)

notes: Highly sought-after celebrity; for an entrepreneurship angle go via Once Upon a Farm's PR firm (ICR). Avoid personal/family topics. Her entertainment publicity is handled separately by her talent reps.

name: Aristeidis P Pittas
current_role: Vice Chairman, Euroseas Ltd. (ESEA) and EuroDry Ltd. (EDRY) and Euroholdings Ltd.; Vice President, Oceanbulk Maritime SA
profile: Aristides P. Pittas (b. ~1951) is a member of the Athens shipping family whose interests were consolidated into Nasdaq-listed Euroseas in 2005; he has been its vice chairman since 2005 and vice chairman of drybulk spin-off EuroDry since 2018. He is a cousin of chairman/CEO Aristides J. Pittas (not to be confused with him) and has been VP of ship manager Oceanbulk Maritime since 1989.
interesting_fact: According to EuroDry's filings he has been a shareholder in over 100 oceangoing vessels over the last 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1979 in the operations and freight-collection department of Gourdomichalis Maritime, then worked four years as a sale-and-purchase ship broker at Trust Marine Enterprises and in the supply department of Drytank SA before joining Oceanbulk in 1989; he holds a BSc in Economics from the Athens School of Economics.
notes: Identity caution: the public face of Euroseas/EuroDry is his cousin Aristides J. Pittas (Chairman/CEO, Lloyd's List Greek Newsmaker 2021); most web bios refer to J., not P. Very low public profile; approach via the company.

name: Jon Halbert
current_role: Director, Caris Life Sciences (Nasdaq: CAI) since 2014; director, Allegiance Group (nonprofit fundraising services)
profile: Jon S. Halbert (66), a Dallas-area healthcare entrepreneur, co-founded pharmacy-benefits manager AdvancePCS with his brother David in 1987 and was its vice chairman until the 2004 merger with Caremark. He later chaired population-health tech firm Phytel until its 2015 sale to IBM, and sits on the board of David's precision-oncology company Caris Life Sciences, which IPO'd in June 2025.
interesting_fact: He chaired Phytel, a provider-led population health technology company, until it was acquired by IBM in 2015 (folded into IBM Watson Health).
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of Forest Forward, a Dallas nonprofit focused on poverty and revitalising South Dallas, and has been on the board of nonprofit fundraising firm Pursuant since 2007; he holds a Bachelor of Accounting from Abilene Christian University.
notes: Brother of Caris founder/CEO David Halbert. Low public profile; no personal channels found. Approach via Caris IR or the nonprofits he supports.

name: Sharon D Garrett
current_role: Independent director, Ross Stores Inc. (since 2000); management consultant (since 2013)
profile: Sharon D. Garrett (77) is a technology and operations executive who was Senior VP and Chief Information Officer of The Walt Disney Company from 1989 to 2000, then EVP Enterprise Services at PacifiCare Health Systems, COO of PT Holdings and an EVP at American Medical Response. She has served on the Ross Stores board since 2000 and now works as a management consultant; her wealth is largely accumulated Ross equity.
interesting_fact: She ran IT for The Walt Disney Company as its CIO for over a decade (1989-2000), then briefly served as interim CEO of Zyan Communications in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: She has sat on the Ross Stores board for more than 25 years, since 2000, and later served on the boards of Jerome's Furniture (chairing its strategic planning committee) and Scott's Liquid Gold.

public_contacts.value: connie.kao@ros.com (Connie Kao, SVP Investor & Media Relations, Ross Stores)

notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Ross IR/media contact is the only published route. Tech-angle: early enterprise CIO; cyber risk expertise per the proxy.

name: Anthony Sun
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Cognex Corporation (since May 2021; director since 1982); former Managing General Partner & CEO, Venrock
profile: Tony Sun (73) is an MIT-trained electrical engineer and Harvard MBA who spent 30+ years at Venrock, the Rockefeller family's venture firm, finishing as managing general partner and CEO before retiring in 2010. He invested in or advised 60+ tech startups, helped start China-focused GGV Capital, and has been on the board of machine-vision company Cognex since 1982, chairing it since founder Bob Shillman retired.
interesting_fact: He has been a Cognex director since 1982, essentially since the machine-vision company's early days, and was in the top ten of the Forbes Midas List in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: He provided the lead gift for the Sun Field Station at Stanford's Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve, and has served as a venture-capital adviser to the US Navy; he holds BS, MS and Engineer degrees in electrical engineering from MIT.
notes: Committee of 100 member since 1997; board of Asian Art Museum of San Francisco. Good fit for a tech/VC history conversation (semiconductors to internet). No personal social accounts found.

name: Matthew J. Hawkins
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Waystar Holding Corp. (Nasdaq: WAY), Lehi, Utah
profile: Matt Hawkins is a BYU and Harvard MBA graduate and ex-McKinsey consultant who ran healthcare software companies for Vista Equity Partners (Greenway Health, Vitera, SirsiDynix) and was president of Sunquest. He formed healthcare-payments software company Waystar in 2017, led its $2.7bn sale to EQT and CPP Investments in 2019 and its 2024 Nasdaq IPO; it now pushes an AI-driven 'autonomous revenue cycle'.
interesting_fact: Waystar's platform processes over 7.5 billion healthcare transactions and more than $2.4 trillion in gross claims a year; under Hawkins it made TIME100 Most Influential Companies and he was named Utah Business CEO of the Year.
deep_cut_fact: Before his private-equity CEO roles he was VP and general manager of Henry Schein Practice Solutions (dental practice-management software) from 2004 to 2007; he graduated from BYU with University Honors.
notes: Media-friendly: has appeared on Bloomberg, CNBC, FOX Business etc. Strong AI/data-infrastructure angle (Waystar partners with Google Cloud). Best route via Waystar communications.
